result.title: Copies Are Not Confirmations: How News Duplication Fools LLM Judges and Continual Learners
result.comment: 19 pages, 13 tables. Code, labels and results: https://github.com/Metalesaek/copies-experiment
result.summary: Many news reports of a claim are copies of one source: wire stories, content shared within a media group, syndicated features and press releases. We ask whether LLM judges and continual learners treat such copies as independent confirmations. In 200,000 English CC-News articles, a MinHash detector links 18.9% to a near-copy from another outlet (precision 0.97 once boilerplate is removed); it links 92% of edited reprints to their originals but none of the LLM rewrites by phi4, Llama 3.2 or Gemini 2.5 Flash. Shown three identical reprints of a claim about an unknown person instead of one report, Llama 3.2 3B and phi4 14B raised the share of lies they accepted from 0.06 to 0.71 and from 0.21 to 0.90 and ignored a note that the reports came from one source; Gemini 2.5 Flash already believed a single report, and Gemini 2.5 Pro followed provenance notes and tables. In a simulated continual-learning stream, showing the judge one report per detected chain cut the copied lies it accepted by 0.10-0.24 across four judges, at a mean cost of no more than 4.2 percentage points of accepted truths. Against reworded copies, a test of how many of a report's named entities are absent from an earlier look-alike separates LLM rewrites from 100 labelled independent reports of the same event with AUC 0.98-0.99 and wrongly flags one; entity overlap alone does as well, TF-IDF and a current embedding model come close, and the test catches few natural same-source derivatives. With the miss patterns of generated rewrite networks, it cut the reworded-copy lies accepted from 0.67 to 0.20 (0.40 when the rewriter invents details). Counting reports or chains alone is not a reliable defence, the effect of provenance information depends on the judge, and colluding sources remain the open problem. Code and labels: https://github.com/Metalesaek/copies-experiment

AI.brief_summary: 论文用 MinHash 在大规模新闻语料中识别近重复报道，测试 LLM 评判器与持续学习模型是否把同一来源的转载误当作独立确认，并提出基于实体缺失和来源链的去重与判别方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「重复证据不等于独立确认」及来源追踪思路，可能启发 LVR 在多条视觉证据或多假设聚合时如何筛除冗余证据、校准置信与停止判断；链级去重和实体缺失检验能否迁移到视觉场景可供核查。
